findings.claim: The decision record is malformed in the store, so the commitment may not be discoverable or enforceable by the very decision system it relies on.
findings.evidence: prior_decisions reports: "skipping malformed entry path=/Users/.../.prometheus/knowledge/wiki/decision-defer-mcp-2026-07-28-adoption.md err=frontmatter parse error: yaml parse: mapping values are not allowed in this context at line 4 column 16". The target document frontmatter has `title: Decision: defer MCP 2026-07-28 adoption; converge rmcp in a dedicated phase`, an unquoted colon-bearing scalar.
findings.suggested_fix: Quote frontmatter values containing colons, rerun ingestion, and verify this decision appears in prior-decision lookup before relying on it as a recorded deferral.

findings.claim: The compatibility evidence does not test the compatibility claim that matters for adoption of MCP 2026-07-28.
findings.evidence: The decision says falsifier 1 was run "against the live rmcp 1.4.0 server" and concludes "The compatibility assumption is now evidence"; the same section admits "Still untested: a real 2026-07-28 server" and the assumptions say acceptance is "not exercised against a live 2026-07-28 server." Testing an old in-stack server negotiating down does not prove old clients will interoperate with a genuine 2026-07-28 server.
findings.suggested_fix: Downgrade the claim to "our current rmcp 1.4.0 server still accepts current clients" and make deferral contingent on an explicit external/genuine 2026-07-28 compatibility test or documented absence of any required 2026-07-28 peer.

findings.claim: The deadline falsifier for "deferring is free" can miss the actual failure modes of deferral.
findings.evidence: Falsifier 3 only fails on "A sixth version or a sixth consumer" or "no convergence phase started" by 2026-08-31. Deferral can still be costly with five versions if an existing consumer breaks, an external 2026-07-28 peer rejects obsolete clients, or the convergence phase starts but does not complete.
findings.suggested_fix: Add falsifiers for failed initialize against required peers, any user-visible MCP regression, and convergence not completed by the deadline rather than merely started.

findings.claim: The decision treats the 12-month deprecation window as load-bearing but does not verify whether the relevant versions are inside that window.
findings.evidence: Assumption: "The 12-month deprecation window holds. From the published policy; not independently confirmed with maintainers." The obsolete client versions are `2025-03-26` and `2025-06-18`, while the decision date is `2026-08-01`; `2025-03-26` is already more than 12 months old at decision time.
findings.suggested_fix: Compute each protocol version's support deadline from the published policy and remove or replace the assumption if any hard-coded version is already outside support.

findings.claim: The rejected protocol-side alternative is dismissed because no end-to-end test exists, but the decision never evaluates the obvious alternative of adding the minimal test instead of deferring.
findings.evidence: Alternative 4 is rejected because "patching a handshake asserts a wire-format change with no end-to-end MCP test in this stack to catch the regression". The decision then says this argues for a later phase, but does not consider "add a minimal initialize compatibility test now, then patch or defer based on it" as an option.
findings.suggested_fix: Add and evaluate a minimal-test-now alternative with estimated effort, and justify why it is larger than the risk accepted by deferral.
